ateret-zekenim/1:_: Therefore it is good to bring the doughs together so they touch one another, as in Yoreh De'ah siman 325; and if each dough has the measure for challah and he wishes to separate from one for the other, he need not combination nor touching — only that both are before him and they separate from one for the other; also in Yoreh De'ah siman 325. And if he wishes to separate challah when they are in a basket or vessel, he should be careful that nothing protrude beyond the sides of the vessel outward, or cover with a cloth — then it is considered like a vessel to combine them. And if he forgot to separate challah from the dough of the matzot, he may wait until night so they will be whole to place on the seder plate; and when he breaks the second matzah for the two [participants] to keep half for afikoman, then he places the two whole matzot and those two broken pieces in a vessel to combine them, covers them, takes a small piece from the broken portion, blesses to separate challah, keeps it until chol ha'moed, and burns it on chol ha'moed (Tur). But it is better to break a small piece for challah immediately and not wait until night, lest he forget also at night — for in any case he will break without a blessing at night (Lechem Rav):
baer-heitev/1:א: (א) To increase. Even if he has many helpers and also two ovens, nevertheless he should not increase the measure of the dough; and if it was more than five or six eggs there is no concern, even for matzah of the mitzvah (Maharil chapter 10):
baer-heitev/1:ג: (3) In a basket. A vessel without receptacle — doubt if combines; covering with cloth counts as vessel and combines — so practice (Taz). Shlah: protest folding dough taking challah from two ends — take one end, one rolls at other end exposed. Custom separate from each dough (Darkei Moshe). Must be per custom of large doughs — Magen Avraham: one blessing suffices all if no unrelated speech between kneading. Now majority separate each dough, each woman blesses. Blessing: no difference Pesach and year (Darkei Moshe; Taz Yoreh De'ah 328). Derishah: reason saying on Pesach "terumat challah matzah from dough" — reason making challah first like matzah then throw to fire; Maharshal house burned without repair — Mateh Moshe; if challah fell in boiling food — besides mixture laws Yoreh De'ah 324, discuss chametz siman 454 seif 3. Kaf HaChayim in father-in-law's name: benefit or keep until after Pesach — see there.
baer-heitev/1:ד: (ד) Not necessary. But both must be placed before him — for although we hold challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate, nevertheless l'chatchila he requires that it be from the surrounding batch (Magen Avraham). And Chayei Adam wrote he need not be from the surrounding batch in challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate — see Acharonim. He wrote in Mishnah Berurah and customs and Levush: if he forgot to separate from the doughs of matzah of the mitzvah he may wait until night so he places them whole on the plate; and when he breaks the second matzah for the two to keep half for afikoman, then he places the two whole matzot and the two broken pieces in a vessel to combine them, covers them, takes a small piece from the broken portion, blesses to separate challah, keeps it for chol ha'moed {it is permitted to benefit while burning it (Maharil); nevertheless it is proper to make a separate bonfire (Mishnah Berurah)} and they burn on chol ha'moed; and it appears to me it is better that he break from it first a small piece immediately by day lest he return and forget — for in any case he will break it without a blessing — end quote. And Kaf HaChayyim wrote so too it is fit to practice not to wait until night — for in any case dough kneaded from erev Yom Tov is forbidden to separate from it on Yom Tov, as written siman 506 — see there {and if there was not in it the measure, so on erev Yom Tov he was not obligated in challah at all, but on Yom Tov through combination they became obligated — certainly he separates from it on Yom Tov}:
baer-heitev/2:א: (א) He should not call. Rather he calls it kochin in a foreign language (Maharil). And it appears to me there is no concern except when its owner calls it by name; but for another, even though he calls it by name, it has no relevance for him, for he has no permission to separate terumah (Magen Avraham):
baer-heitev/2:ג: (ג) To burn. For one does not burn kodshim on Yom Tov:
baer-heitev/2:ד: (ד) To cool. Magen Avraham wrote — requires study whether one may rely on this at this time, since even those cooling who stand a little in the house become warm — see there; and Kaf HaChayyim permits plainly. {And in Pri Chadash he concludes they become warm somewhat — one should exchange them; see Yoreh De'ah siman 36 — see there}:
baer-heitev/2:ה: (ה) Minor. Less than nine years (Darkei Moshe; Mahariv). Magen Avraham explained: we say presumably he did not see keri; but if we know he saw keri, even a one-day-old is impure for his keri — end quote. And it escaped him the sugya of the Gemara beginning chapter Bnot Kutim, and Rambam explicitly chapter 9 of Laws of Fathers of Impurity: less than a nine-year-old, even if he lay with a woman and saw keri, he does not become impure (Chayei Adam):
baer-heitev/2:ז: (ז) Kohen. For we do not treat him as a kohen — certainly lest he became profaned (Maharshal; Maharil); see Shach Yoreh De'ah siman 322 who wrote that on Pesach they practice giving to a minor kohen, unlike all year — and Magen Avraham gave the reason. And in these countries I have seen the practice to burn the challah by reciting aloud or on chol ha'moed. And on Yom Tov he does not call a name until after baking, which is more correct (Chayei Adam):
beer-hagolah/1:ב: (Explanation: they should adhere to one another — Beit Yosef)
beer-hagolah/2:ב: (Rosh, in the name of Rabbenu Tam:)
beer-hagolah/1:ג: Statement of Rav Yosef; and per R' Eliezer in Pesachim — Magen Avraham in Mishnah Pesachim 46; and per R' Eliezer
biur-halacha/1:א: (א) And it is better to reduce it — see Chok Yaakov; and I copied above in siman 456 in Mishna Berurah s.k. 7 that if he has only one dough it is good not to diminish so as not to lose challah, and he is the number of terumah — see there in Sha'arei Tzedek:
biur-halacha/1:ב: (ב) That he place all the matzot in a basket — and a tray that has no waste, such as a table, is in doubt; therefore when combining them in a vessel he should be careful that nothing go above the sides of the vessel, as stated in Yoreh De'ah siman 325 seif 1 in the gloss. And b'dieved if he did not cover them and took from the upper ones — challah on the whole basket: Peri Megadim is uncertain whether it helps; and in my humble opinion it appears one need not be stringent b'dieved, since in any case the view of Semag is to be lenient that covering is not required, for the air of the vessel combines them since the vessel has an interior even what protrudes above is considered as placed below — and his view was brought in Biur HaGra there — see there:
biur-halacha/1:ג: (ג) And the basket combines them for challah — the same applies through covering with a cloth; that is, he places them on a cloth and places this cloth also over the matzot from above; and even though in the middle some are exposed, all combine since from the sides they are covered — end quote Peri Megadim; and this flows from Shach Yoreh De'ah in the name of Maharil; and Peri Megadim concludes: therefore if placed on a tray and above with a cloth — no. And in my humble opinion one should study the fundamental law, for in Semak it is implied that plain covering also helps — see there; and so in Machatzit HaShekel it is implied that through plain covering it helps — requires study for practice. Indeed in a vessel that has an interior, only that the matzot protrude above — in this it certainly appears one may be lenient through plain covering, after Semag is completely lenient, as above. And know: if we say plain cloth covering helps to combine, the same if he inverted a vessel over the matzot it also helps to combine; indeed per this, what R' Eliezer said — even one who winnows and puts into a basket etc. — is not precise, for the same if he inverted the basket over them:
chatam-sofer/1:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 5 he reconciles it and it is non-sacred. Note: one who makes an agent to separate — who reconciles? See responsa Chatam Sofer Yoreh De'ah siman 320 {and he wrote the matter is simple that both may ask the agent and the homeowner, except if the agent asks about his vow and regrets from the outset about what he gave his mind to separate — from this side the vow is uprooted from its root and he returns to tithe it; then he returns and separates another terumah, for he still did not perform his agency at all, for the first separation is like the act of a monkey in the world; not so when the homeowner regrets — he must regret the essence of what he gave his mind based on the mind of this agent, and if so automatically the first agency is void and he must appoint an agent anew, etc.; and from being good they should annul vows for both of them, the agent and the homeowner}:
chatam-sofer/2:_: {in Magen Avraham s.k. 7} Even if he is a son, etc. Note: this is not so, as Kaf HaChayyim wrote — see there. And on erev Pesach that falls on Shabbat see below siman 506 in Magen Avraham s.k. 8 and what I wrote in the margin:
chok-yaakov/1:ג: Good to bring doughs together. Do not leave dough folded when separating — take from one end, one arranges with roller at other end exposed (Shlah). Custom separate each dough (Darkei Moshe) — per custom large doughs as siman 456 above. Magen Avraham: one blessing if no unrelated speech; now majority separate, each woman blesses; make challah first like matzah then throw to fire; some burn without repair; if fell in dish — challah mixture Yoreh De'ah 324 and chametz siman 454 note 4.
chok-yaakov/1:ד: (ד) To bring the doughs together. So they adhere to one another, that if he wishes to separate one from the other he tears one slightly from its companion and then all is considered one dough; and when he takes challah from one of them it suffices. Indeed I saw they practice cutting one piece from both together — and this is seemingly a custom without reason. {See Beit Yosef in what he wrote in the name of an Ashkenazic responsum, and it is in a responsum to Rashba, and in responsum of Maharam bar Baruch siman 262, that it is implied somewhat that we require cutting from each dough and each dough — also in this they challenged him; and all the more so in Behag that all is considered one piece and one dough.} And from my master the exalted Rav R' Yosef I heard the reason: sometimes the doughs are hard and do not adhere together through proximity alone, as Taz and Rosh Yosef wrote; and through the strength of the cutting that they cut from both they adhere to one another — and this is a correct reason:
chok-yaakov/1:ה: (ה) And if impossible. It is implied that whenever possible to separate from the dough it is preferable, for the essence of the mitzvah is to separate from the dough, as written "the first of your doughs." And that which we say in the chapter Elu Overin that the women of his household practiced l'chatchila to act per R' Eliezer through combining another basket after baking — this too deals where it was impossible because of haste and the like; and this is simple and settled in what Netziv left in his timna on Tur and Mechaber in s.k. 1 — examine:
chok-yaakov/1:ו: (ו) He separates it after baking immediately. For although we hold challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate — this is in dough kneaded together that was already connected; they were lenient in challah of chutz la'aretz that we do not require separating from the surrounding batch, only eat and go and afterward separate; not so here. And so is the language of Tosafot first chapter of Niddah daf 7a end s.v. umekafet — see there; and it is implied there from Tosafot that even in two doughs where each had the measure, if he wishes to separate one for all of them we require surrounding — even in challah of chutz la'aretz, for Shmuel did not say eat and go except in one dough that became obligated in challah; and so Bach in s.k. 4. And with this the words of Rosh and Tur are very well settled, and he escapes all the difficulties Taz s.k. 4 raised on the words of Rosh and Tur against each other — for that which Rosh and Tur required surrounding even in challah of chutz la'aretz deals only with two doughs where each has the measure for challah and he wishes to separate terumah from one for its fellow; unlike Magen Avraham in s.k. 3 who challenged Bach on this, that he wrote the implication of Rosh's language is chapter Elu Overin deals with one dough — and this is not so, even though he used the term "dough," meaning in one dough there was the measure for challah; nevertheless it deals that afterward he wishes to combine another dough; and so explained explicitly in Kitzur Peskei HaRosh that therefore he required surrounding there {and nevertheless b'dieved if he forgot and ate he separates afterward, even in two doughs where each had the measure — only that l'chatchila we require surrounding per Tur and Rosh in chapter Elu Overin, as Bach explained, and this is correct for one who studies there; but if the doughs are not of the measure and he ate, even b'dieved the separation afterward does not help, since he did not combine them together — then he was not obligated in challah at all unless he left from each a piece and a piece and combined them}. And so explained in Yoreh De'ah siman 323 in Shulchan Aruch in the gloss, and in Beit Yosef in the name of Semag and in Hagahot Maimoniot and from the words of Tosafot and Rosh first chapter of Beitzah brought in Beit Yosef below siman 506. And so in Hagahot Semak and Mordechai and Agudah chapter 1 of Yom Tov. And in Shiltei HaGibborim in the name of Sefer HaTerumah — and all this is simple and clear and settled in the words of Rosh and Tur in their words, and explicitly so in Kitzur Peskei HaRosh; and in vain did all these Acharonim toil, and especially Taz in s.k. 4 who challenged Rosh and Tur in all this — and in truth it is wondrous and requires study:
chok-yaakov/1:ז: (ז) All the matzot in a basket. Bach wrote: per Rosh in laws of challah and Tosafot chapter Elu Overin (Pesachim daf 47) in Tosafot s.v. heveil requires also touching one another; and it must be said Tur abbreviated here and Taz lengthened to challenge him on this from the words of Tosafot chapter 1 of Overin; and this caused him all this — that the supplement of first chapter of Niddah daf 7a at length escaped him {for in Tosafot chapter Elu Overin they greatly abbreviated the supplement; therefore one can explain per Taz's view, not so in the supplement of Niddah} that they wrote explicitly: and it is correct on Pesach to touch all the matzot in the basket when separating one for all, for the basket does not combine them; and even though we say challah of chutz la'aretz eat and go, etc. — behold explicitly from the words of the supplement that even in matzot where the obligation comes through combination, nevertheless touching one another is required; and so explained there in Peskei Tosafot and in Agudah in the name of R' Yitzchak. Even though there it is explained from the beginning of their words that we do not require touching where it is not of the measure and the basket combines them — nevertheless this is if he wishes only combination of the measure; not so in matzot where after baking three or four doughs and combining them together, through combination there are here two or three doughs of the measure for challah and he wishes to separate terumah from the surrounding batch from one for its fellow — therefore touching one another is required to exempt through one challah, as above per Tosafot's view; and especially for one who studies Peskei Tosafot and Agudah; and not as Maharam explained — a strange and forced explanation of Tosafot's view; also Maharsha appears to emend somewhat in Tosafot and is forced in their view; and in truth Tosafot's words are simple and clear, as written. It is found Bach aimed correctly at Tosafot's view; and nevertheless Tosafot's view and Rosh's are not equal, as Bach's implication — for Rosh in laws of challah ruled explicitly to the contrary: if he wishes to combine for the measure he requires touching; not so if there were in two doughs each the measure for challah and he wishes to separate terumah from the surrounding batch from one for its fellow — he need not touching nor basket-combination, only proximity one to the other; and he rejects there the proof of Tosafot in chapter Elu Overin; and so in Shiltei HaGibborim siman 60 in the name of Sefer HaTerumah; and so Rashba ruled in his Peskei Challah; and so implied in responsa of Rashba siman 374; and so Agudah chapter Elu Overin in the name of Terumat HaDeshen and Ravyah — specifically where he is particular about mixture, such as one dough impure and pure and the like, touching is required {and in Agudah there he wrote basket-combination helps per Geonim even without touching}; and so Kol Bo daf 49d: the air of the vessel combines and touching is not required at all — and this is Tur and Shulchan Aruch's view, that they did not mention touching at all; therefore it appears to me that although l'chatchila touching is required, b'dieved it is valid and we may rely on great poskim who did not require touching at all; and so if there were in two doughs the measure for challah, b'dieved he need not even basket-combination, and all the more so touching — only proximity one to the other, as Rosh's explicit language in laws of challah; but l'chatchila one should practice and require touching; and so Maharshal in responsum siman 58: even if there was in the dough the measure and he forgot to separate, l'chatchila we require basket-combination and touching. However the Rav's view in the gloss is not so, as it is implied explicitly that in such a case even basket-combination is not required — see there in Tosafot Niddah that they left in requires study whether touching alone is considered like basket-combination or biting; and so in Agudah:
chok-yaakov/1:ח: (ח) And even basket-combination. And he need not separate terumah from the surrounding batch that they be touching one to the other, for challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate, as written in s.k. 6; see Yoreh De'ah siman 323; and see what is written nearby in the name of Maharshal in responsum:
chok-yaakov/1:ט: And from part did not take. Mateh Moshe, minhagim, Levush: if forgot from matzah of mitzvah doughs, wait until night to place whole on plate; when breaking second matzah for two for afikoman, place two whole and two broken in vessel to combine, cover, take small piece from broken, bless challah, keep for chol ha'moed, burn chol ha'moed. Better break small piece by day lest forget — anyway breaks without blessing at night — Levush; so practice not wait until night — dough from erev Yom Tov forbidden separate on Yom Tov siman 506; brother-in-law wondered permitting night Yom Tov — if forgot until night, for those not kneading challah measure together, no obligation erev — obligated now on Yom Tov through combination — permit separate Yom Tov though could combine erev (unlike kneading warm bread) — as Levush siman 506; nevertheless permit Yom Tov since not dipped until now — Beitzah 2a explicitly; thus answer Levush difficulty; if forgot, lenient more — Magen Avraham siman 506 note 10; also eat guarded matzah. Nevertheless what can separate before night without doubt, do not be lenient gratuitously.
chok-yaakov/2:א: It becomes chametz. Although holy and no bal yera'eh bal yimatzei — since if he wishes he redeems it — Pesachim 46; therefore Erev Pesach on Shabbos with chametz challah already ate chametz — cannot redeem, ate tevel retroactively (Yoreh De'ah 323); vows not asked on Shabbos if not Shabbos need — siman 341; no destruction needed since no bal yera'eh even breaking vessel — Pesachim 6a separated; although challah now d'rabbanan, d'oraisa bal yera'eh bal yimatzei — we hold d'oraisa nullification suffices — study. If minor kohen or kohen immersed for keri, may eat — below; at least press vessel.
chok-yaakov/2:ב: (ב) He places it to cool. Magen Avraham wrote — requires study whether one may rely on this at this time, since even those cooling, if they stand a little in the house, become warm — end quote; and I do not know what his doubt is in a matter that was permitted plainly in the Gemara and all poskim first and last did not mention this stringency; and if the time is hot there is a remedy to act as explained above beginning siman 455 seif 1:
chok-yaakov/2:ג: (ג) Minor. That is, a nine-year-old who presumably did not see keri; but if we know, even a one-day-old is impure for his keri — end quote Magen Avraham. And in truth this is a great error, for in truth from Mahariv brought in Beit Yosef he understood per the rush incorrectly; but the truth is not so, and it escaped him the sugya of the Gemara beginning chapter Bnot Kutim and Rambam explicitly chapter 5 of Laws of Fathers of Impurity: less than a nine-year-old, even if he lay with a woman and saw keri, he does not become impure — and this is from the Torah's decree; and that which Mahariv wrote that impurity does not leave his body — this means even if keri leaves from him he is not impure:
chok-yaakov/2:ד: (ד) Who immersed for his keri. See Yoreh De'ah siman 322 that some require also sunset; see Rambam in the law of immersion for keri:
chok-yaakov/2:ה: (ה) It is permitted to bake the challah for him. Per what was ruled in Yoreh De'ah siman 323 that it is permitted l'chatchila to nullify it in the majority in challah nowadays; and if so, even if there is no pure kohen here, it is also permitted to bake it, since he can nullify it; see Beit Yosef — see there in Shach. Maharil and Maharash wrote: one need not a separate bonfire or bonfires of a kohen to burn it, for even he himself is permitted to nullify it in the majority for eating by non-kohanim — and all the more so it is permitted to benefit from it; and nevertheless he concludes it is proper to make a separate bonfire or the oven in which they bake before they lowered the matzot into it — and so they practice, or they place it on the fire before the oven; see Shach in Yoreh De'ah siman 322:
chok-yaakov/2:ז: (ז) That it is permitted on Yom Tov to knead less than the measure. Taz wrote: and he should not knead at all anymore; and if he kneads another dough less than the measure, there is concern lest they combine afterward in one vessel and come to obligation and eat tevel — end quote; and this concern is remote in challah of chutz la'aretz that is d'rabbanan, for certainly if they combine he will also separate his challah, as written above s.k. 2 that we are not concerned for this except if he separated once from a dough that was less than the measure, as Rosh brought above s.k. 2; see responsum of Maharshal siman 58 that he wrote if he takes the challah after baking he must take a whole matzah, and we do not practice so — only break a piece from them; see Yoreh De'ah:
chokhmat-shlomo/1:_: Seif 2: One should not call name until baked, etc. Gemara Pesachim 42b and R' Chananel: that foreskin — since obligation, bar kapparah; challenge: for Rabbah reverse — here lacking act, there not — for R' Chananel internal difficulty; say R' Chananel has hu'il only leniently, stringent too; proven there when not lacking act, stringent all say hu'il. Study from Makkot 13b: for R' Akiva if did not repent, liable keraitot now; why not answer perhaps repented — because hu'il; if repents not two wickednesses — lashes; hu'il stringent, not lacking act — Kiddushin: righteous even if wicked perhaps thought repentance; why not hu'il here — great question. In hu'il sugya R' Yehoshua: good of benefit not money; She'eilat Ya'avetz chametz: Bava Metzia proves R' Yehoshua holds good of benefit is money — I expanded elsewhere; now appears: R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua dispute if good of benefit is money — not logic, whether Torah made it like money; one: since Torah gave him to separate, made like money; one: Torah did not. chametz: like R' Eliezer — not in his possession, Torah made as if in possession; actual money Torah made as if possession — all year not in possession, Torah as if possession — actual money; benefit Torah made like money — acquired now; Torah did not make still as if possession — established; benefit not actually money — clear; study well. (Same seif) {Rama: if minor kohen who did not see keri or adult immersed for keri may bake challah for him.} See Magen Avraham Rivan, Darkei Moshe: less than nine; wrote: we say presumably no keri; if saw keri even day-old impure — Kaf HaChayim objected: under nine even if saw keri not impure — see my Niddah; now Rambam Terumot 7: minor who did not see keri, minor who did not see niddah blood — eat always without checking, presumption no impurity yet — therefore Rivan, Darkei Moshe until nine; Rambam must mean under nine; nevertheless wrote presumption — if known impurity, forbidden like adult tamei — Magen Avraham. Therefore Kaf HaChayim opposite — Rambam means distinction: impure others by touch not, but from his body tamei — clear proof. Study well. Now Rambam Tum'at Met 1:14: adult and minor become impure all impurities — "all" includes keri; not only met but all — gentiles and animals not; gezeirah gentiles like zavim; why zav here — only met? Must include zav in "all" — therefore minors impure all including keri from body — Magen Avraham. Forced: minor nine years — all impurities even day-old; if "all" includes keri from body — Magen Avraham. Forced under nine — Makkot 27 Rashi s.v. kohen katan: not impure from body; if immersed like kohen katan for keri — alternative; Bechorot 27 Leshonot Rashi — dispute Magen Avraham/Kaf HaChayim; under nine even keri not impure others — Leshonot Bach; Rosh challah agrees touch required; our master abbreviated — Tosafot Eruvin 46: in basket touch required for surrounding challah; Tur, Shulchan Aruch did not require touch here — we hold not from surrounding Yoreh De'ah 323; R' Yonatan in Semag: basket does not combine — Peri Megadim uncertain; appears no stringent b'dieved since Semag lenient air of vessel combines interior even above — Biur HaGra; study Yoreh De'ah 325.
dagul-merevavah/1:_: I do not know from where he derived this; and in tractate Niddah daf 32 it is implied specifically in ziva a minor one-day-old becomes impure, but in keri we require nine years and one day; and so explained explicitly in Rambam chapter 5 of Laws of Other Fathers of Impurity halakhah 2; see Rambam first chapter of Laws of Impurity of Bedding halakhah 4:
eshel-avraham/1:א: (א) One to the other. And in Yoreh De'ah siman 485 it is implied touching is required in a manner that if they separate, one tears slightly with it — see there:
eshel-avraham/1:ב: (ב) Correct. Bach in the name of Rosh wrote it is better through wetting, as above — see there his reason. And that which we hold challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate — it is implied we do not require from the surrounding batch; this is in dough kneaded together — they were lenient within twelve hours; see Niddah chapter 4:
eshel-avraham/2:א: It becomes chametz. Although holy and not his — since if he wishes redeems — Erev Pesach Shabbos chametz challah ate chametz — cannot redeem, ate tevel (Yoreh De'ah 323); vows not on Shabbos if not need — 341; no biur — no bal yera'eh even break vessel — Pesachim 6a; challah d'rabbanan, chametz d'oraisa — d'oraisa nullification suffices; if minor kohen or immersed kohen, eat — see there.
eshel-avraham/2:ב: (ד) Who immersed. And he should not bake first, for it lacks action — not so, since we also do not permit, lest a kohen come (Pri Chadash) — see there:
kaf-hachayyim/1:_: (1) [Seif 1] Because one must be careful, etc. The practice in most places is to appoint a supervisor over making the matzot to stand over their making and to urge those engaged in them; and it is simply that this requires a wise, understanding, Heaven-fearing man; and for such matters one does not make a group of women and minors. Sefer HaZikaronot daf 24b. Knesset HaGedolah in Hagahot Tosefta; see below siman 464 or 11:
levushei-serad/1:_: Taz s.k. 2 — only that it requires all the ways of combination, as should be read:
levushei-serad/2:_: Magen Avraham s.k. 3 — and he wrote to distinguish between two doughs; and it is difficult, for Rosh chapter 3 of Pesachim, etc. — as should be read:
machatzit-hashekel/1:א: (s.k. 1) Good, etc. And some place, etc. Shlah wrote the error spread from what Shulchan Aruch wrote "therefore good to bring the doughs together" — and it was exchanged for them between "doughs" and "dough," and they thought it means to bring the second ends of the dough together. And they did not act well, because the dough warms in this rubbing when they rub their hands in joining the dough from end to end around the roller — end quote; see Yoreh De'ah siman 19 — as should be read regarding if he already separated from one dough and before separating from the second dough there is dispute of poskim there regarding the blessing; such is the case here in slaughter, and the same here:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ב: (Siman 330 s.k. 3-4) He wrote the reason, etc. Since Tur brought there section 11 that all year one must separate terumah — it must be explicit in the language of the blessing the name of the mitzvah; and challah means cake; therefore one must say terumah, for such is the name of the mitzvah:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ג: (As it is written: challah you shall raise — terumah.) Behold its name is terumah, only that terumah shall be challah. And it is that all year they are not particular about this and say to separate challah; nevertheless on Pesach they are more particular to say terumah, since then they make thin matzot like a cake; if he would say to separate challah — meaning cake — it would not be clear at all in the language of the blessing, for all the matzot are cakes; therefore on Pesach they are more particular to say terumah. And nevertheless they also say the word challah — it must be for the change in the blessing between the text of all year, where they also say the word challah as all year, only they add the word terumah. First like matzah:
machatzit-hashekel/1:ו: However Maharshal wrote in responsum siman 58 that since basket-combination is required as Shulchan Aruch wrote, then he must separate a whole challah — see there his reason:
magen-avraham/1:א: Good to bring the doughs together. And some place the dough folded at the time of separating challah — and this is not correct (Shlah). The custom is to separate from each dough and each dough alone (Darkei Moshe). And nevertheless one blessing suffices for all if he did not interrupt between them with speech unrelated to kneading (Yoreh De'ah siman 19; and see what is written siman 330). Regarding the blessing there is no difference between Pesach and other days of the year (Darkei Moshe section 38). And in Derishah Yoreh De'ah siman 328 he wrote the reason for those who practice saying on Pesach "terumat challah matzah from the dough" — see there; and he also gave a reason why they practice making it first like matzah and afterward throwing it into the fire; and he concludes that in the house of Maharshal they practiced burning it without repair — and so Matanot Kehunah:
magen-avraham/1:ג: Not required. But both must be placed before him — for although we hold challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate, nevertheless l'chatchila he requires from the surrounding batch (as Tur and per Rosh's view chapter 3 of Pesachim). Bach challenged: behold Tur Yoreh De'ah wrote it is permitted to eat l'chatchila and afterward separate; and he wrote to distinguish between two doughs — and Rosh chapter 3 of Pesachim deals with one dough, for he disagrees with Rashi — see there; and it appears to distinguish: in any case the challah with what he separates from it requires from the surrounding batch (see Noda B'Yehuda). Maharil wrote it is permitted to burn it in an Israelite bonfire, for Rashi ruled an Israelite is permitted to eat it through nullification in the majority, and it is fit to rely on him to benefit from it; see Yoreh De'ah siman 323; and some are stringent:
magen-avraham/2:א: He should not call a name. Rather he calls it kochin in a foreign language (Maharil). And it appears to me there is no concern except when its owner calls it by name; but for another, even though he calls it by name, it has no relevance for him, for he has no permission to separate terumah:
magen-avraham/2:ו: That we do not feed. For we do not treat him as a kohen — certainly lest one of his mothers became profaned (Maharshal; Maharil); and Shach in Yoreh De'ah siman 322 wrote a reason is needed why on Pesach they practice giving challah to a minor, and on other days of the year they do not practice giving to a minor — end quote; and it is possible because the challot are numerous, and if they do not eat them they will not treat him as a kohen, as Rashi wrote in Chullin chapter 18 regarding priestly gifts:
mechaber/1:main: The law of conduct regarding challah from matzah dough. It contains 2 seifim. Because one must be careful with the measure of the dough not to make it too large, from concern for chimutz, and it is better to reduce it somewhat; therefore it is good to bring the doughs together at the time of separating challah so they touch one another, lest one of them did not have the requisite measure. If it is impossible to separate challah while still dough because of haste, he separates it immediately after baking, when he places all the matzot in a basket — and the basket combines them for challah; and this is the most correct way. {Rama: And if there was the measure for challah and he forgot to separate, he separates afterward; and even basket-combination is not required. If he took from part of the doughs and from part he did not take and they became mixed, he must take challah from each one individually, or knead another dough and take from it also for those that became mixed. If he recognizes one matzah that is obligated in challah, he takes from it for the others (Hagahot Maimoniot chapter 3, and Mordechai beginning of chapter Elu Overin, and Beit Yosef in the name of Tosafot first chapter of Beitzah).}
mechaber/2:main: One who kneads dough on Pesach Yom Tov should not pronounce the name upon it for challah until it is baked. For if he pronounces the name upon it, he is not permitted to bake it; and if he leaves it so it will become chametz, and he is not permitted to burn it on Yom Tov. If he forgot and pronounced the name upon it, he places it to cool and prevents it from becoming chametz. {Rama: And if there is a minor kohen who has not seen keri, or an adult who immersed for his keri, it is permitted to bake the challah for him (Tur). And some say one does not feed challah at this time to any kohen (Mahariv). Some say it is permitted on Yom Tov to knead less than the measure in order to exempt oneself from challah (Ran beginning chapter Elu Overin).}
mishnah-berurah/1:ד: (ד) Lest perhaps there is, etc. — meaning: if so, when he separates challah with a blessing his blessing will be in vain; and further we are concerned lest some of the doughs do not have the measure for challah — then their separation is nothing; and perhaps afterward after baking he will put them into the matzot in one vessel and they will combine and become obligated in challah by law, and he will end up eating tevel. And in a place where the world practices kneading large doughs of the measure for challah, as brought at the end of the previous siman in Mishna Berurah, they separate challah from each dough and each dough separately; and they practice that from each dough and each dough a different woman separates and blesses for herself. And if one person separates for all the doughs, one blessing suffices for all if he did not interrupt between them with speech unrelated to kneading. Acharonim wrote that the custom some practice to fold the dough at the time of separation in order to separate challah from two ends is a custom that is not correct; it suffices to separate from one end:
mishnah-berurah/1:ו: (ו) After baking immediately when he places, etc. — and so too in challah of chutz la'aretz; and even though in challah of chutz la'aretz of eat and go and leaving some for challah — this is in one large dough, even though afterward divided into several loaves, since at first they were connected from one dough they were lenient in chutz la'aretz that we do not require surrounding and connected at the time of separation; not so here, where they are from separate doughs, even though placed one by one in a basket — nevertheless it is not like complete connection to be lenient to eat before separation. And even if each dough had the measure for challah, we also require that it be from the surrounding batch at the time of separation, since they are not from one dough, as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 323 seif 1 in the gloss:
mishnah-berurah/1:כ: (יא) From each one individually — for if he takes from one there is concern lest this is from that which was already exempted, and then it would be from the exempt upon the obligated:
mishnah-berurah/2:ג: (16) It becomes chametz — although holy not his — violates bal yera'eh since if he wishes redeems — becomes non-sacred.
mishnah-berurah/2:ז: (כ) And if there is a kohen, etc. — the Mechaber deals with challah of Eretz Yisrael that is not eaten by kohanim nowadays, since we are all impure from the dead and the challah became impure and forbidden to feed even a pure kohen; therefore it is forbidden to bake it on Yom Tov in every case; therefore he did not mention these details. And Rama deals with challah of chutz la'aretz that is forbidden only to one from whom impurity leaves his body, such as a zav or ba'al keri; but a pure kohen from zav and keri, such as a minor kohen less than nine years and one day who does not become impure from keri, and also presumptively did not see ziva since he is less than nine, or an adult who immersed for his keri — is permitted to eat challah of chutz la'aretz, as written in Yoreh De'ah siman 322; therefore Rama wrote if there is a minor kohen, etc., that even though he called it by the name challah, he is permitted to bake even on Yom Tov, since it is fit for eating:
mishnah-berurah/2:ט: (כב) That we do not feed, etc. — for we do not treat him as a kohen — certainly lest one of his mothers became profaned. And nevertheless for law, the Rav's view is as the first opinion that they give to a minor or to an adult who immersed for his keri [Shach in Yoreh De'ah siman 322 letter 9]. And Peri Megadim wrote: nevertheless I have not seen practicing so even on Pesach. And in our countries there are some places where they give to an adult kohen who immersed for his keri on Pesach; see Magen Avraham who wrote the reason why specifically on Pesach the custom is to give:
netiv-chayim/1:_: (Magen Avraham s.k. 3) For in Tur it is written permitted, etc., and Rosh first chapter of Beitzah supports one dough — Maharil, as should be read:
peri-megadim/1:_: Good — Taz and Kaf HaChayyim letter 4 that they cut from both together and thereby the dough adhered together even in hard dough. And in Yoreh De'ah there, specifically min b'mino — see there in siman 325 in Taz and Shach 1, and in siman 324 in Taz 2. And it appears the same for vessel-combination — specifically one species; two species — no; and all the more so from dough, for per the first tanna second chapter of Menachot the basket does not combine; however one may say in dough he is particular, not so in basket-combination after baking, and touching does not matter — it is implied even in two species it combines; and see section 4 Magen Avraham — it is implied basket-combination too we require min b'mino; and it is forced to say per the view that we require biting — see section 2 Menachot — see there; requires study. And Ra'avad there explained min b'mino — basket-combination; and again in several places in chapter 6 of Laws of Bechoros section 17 in the name of Rashba z"l that in a basket too min b'mino specifically; and it appears from what Ra'avad wrote there impure and pure — see there. A vessel that has no waste is in doubt — end quote Menachot section 17; and challah of chutz la'aretz that is d'rabbanan — doubt for leniency; and the same now in challah of Eretz Yisrael — end quote there; and in Yoreh De'ah 322 in Shach 4. And if he placed matzot in a basket and the upper ones are not within the partitions of the basket — there is doubt whether it is like siman 325 seif 1 in the gloss and Shach 4 and Taz 2; and if he took from the upper ones — challah on the whole basket: seemingly doubt d'rabbanan for leniency, for perhaps a tray that has no waste combines all upper and lower together, and he took obligation upon obligation; and one wise man told me there is no doubt removing from certainty, for the lower ones were already obligated through basket-combination, and doubt whether separated from obligation upon them. And behold in Shulchan Aruch he wrote: some say in d'rabbanan doubt removes from certainty — see Mikvaot: an impure person descended to immerse — see Kaf HaChayyim. And behold one may say doubt of presumptive prohibition in d'rabbanan is stringent in doubt of action, not in doubt of inquiry; and dispute of rabbis — for because of presumption the law should not change; why in remaining few signs — see Kaf HaChayyim; and here one should not elaborate; and it appears to take from the lower ones without a blessing — requires study, lest he come to separate for another place; and covering with a cloth means he places them on a cloth and places this cloth also over the matzot; and if placed on a tray and above with a cloth — not so, as siman 325 section 5 — meaning with one cloth below and above; and even though in the middle some are exposed, all combine since from the sides they are covered:
peri-megadim/2:_: Lest perhaps — Taz's general intent: kneading two doughs, and in each the measure — he must surround one to the other somewhat, adjacent, that he separate from one for its fellow; not so when there is not in each the measure for challah, and through vessel-combination they became obligated — he need not from the surrounding batch; therefore they did not mention surrounding here. And Tosafot in Elu Overin 46b s.v. heveil: in a basket touching is required — when there is in each the measure for challah that requires surrounding, then basket and touching are required; not like Rosh that surrounding alone suffices; or Tosafot also hold basket is not required — only touching, for basket does not help and touching is also required; and this in challah of chutz la'aretz that is d'rabbanan — then there is a difference between when there is in each the measure for challah, surrounding is required to separate from one for all, and when there is not in each the measure for challah, only through combination — then surrounding is not required; therefore challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate, since it was from one dough; and Kaf HaChayyim letter 2; and from challah of chutz la'aretz of eat and afterward separate we are not concerned he forgot, for he is mindful. Not so if he separates from each dough alone, lest among them there is one not obligated in challah and the separation is void, and afterward in the basket they become obligated and he will not separate and eat tevel; see Ra'avad's explanation chapter 2 of Challah mishnah 4: surrounding does not require touching; and nevertheless impure and pure require touching — and implied even when each has the measure; and implied when there is not in each the measure, actual basket and touching are required to combine the measure for challah; and on Yom Tov there — understand; see R' Shimshon there; and see in letter 5 it will be explained further:
rabbi-akiva-eiger/2:_: And so ruled Maharshal and Maharil in Yeshuot Yaakov Chullin chapter 25:
turei-zahav/1:א: Good to bring the doughs together. Beit Yosef wrote the doughs should touch one another until a little adheres from one to the other; and so wrote Rabbenu in Yoreh De'ah siman 325 — end quote; and in the Gemara it states in the language "they bite one another"; and in Yoreh De'ah siman 325 I brought the words of Tur HaDeshen that touching is required so that if they separate, one tears slightly from its companion; and if so, any dough kneaded hard, even though placed one by one, do not adhere together and there is no combination here — therefore one acts through vessel-combination. Beit Yosef wrote: a vessel that has no receptacle — Rambam wrote there is doubt whether it combines; and if one covers the bread with a cloth it is considered like a vessel and they combine — therefore one should act so:
turei-zahav/1:ב: Lest perhaps one of them, etc. Concern lest later obligated through combination and eats tevel — Rosh Beitzah 1 as nearby. Mahari Weil: seemingly our master basket helps even without touch; Yoreh De'ah 325 plainly basket combines; Semak requires touch; Tosafot Pesachim 46 s.v. heveil; Rosh challah agrees touch required. Our master abbreviated — Tosafot: in basket touch required for surrounding challah; Tur, Shulchan Aruch did not require touch — we hold not from surrounding 323; R' Yonatan Semag basket not combine — Peri Megadim uncertain; no stringent b'dieved — Semag lenient vessel air combines — Biur HaGra; study 325.
turei-zahav/2:א: He is not permitted to bake it. For it is not fit for eating:
turei-zahav/2:ב: And he is not permitted to burn it. For one does not burn kodshim on Yom Tov; and Tur concludes here: therefore he should not call it by name until after baking, and then combine everything in the basket and separate one for all — end quote. And requires study: behold initially there was in the dough the measure for challah, for he kneaded only one dough; if so basket-combination is not required, only plain surrounding, as Tur himself wrote before this — basket-combination is required only when there was not the measure for challah, then the basket combines everything for challah; not so in obligation of surrounding when there is the measure for challah; and it appears Tur cited combination here but intended they be close to one another; and if so, even when placed adjacent one to the other, even on the table, it suffices; and there is room to study in what is implied that there is obligation to surround when there is the measure for challah, as Tur wrote before this — rather he brings all the loaves together, etc.; and in Be'er Sheva first chapter of Beitzah it is written: however surrounding we certainly do not require, since he permits in challah of chutz la'aretz: eat and go and afterward separate; and what they practiced on Pesach to place all the matzot in one vessel — not because of surrounding, etc., as written nearby; and if so why did Tur write in this siman that we require surrounding, and he also brings the law of challah of chutz la'aretz eat and go — it is implied even l'chatchila we do not require surrounding, for when he separates afterward the challah on what he eats, behold there is no surrounding; and in truth one may say so also on Rosh, who wrote in chapter 1 of Overin: when there is the measure for challah, basket-combination is not required, only plain surrounding — from which we learn surrounding is in any case required here; one may say there he deals with explaining R' Eliezer's words who said the basket combines them for challah, and the tanna in chapter 1 of Overin deals that we require surrounding — and he does not deal there with challah of chutz la'aretz; but on Tur it is difficult, for he required surrounding — it is implied even in chutz la'aretz; and this contradicts what he wrote afterward eat and go, etc.; and one may explain Rosh's words without Tur: in chapter 1 of Overin it deals when there are two doughs where each has the measure for challah and he wishes to separate from one for its fellow — in this surrounding is required; for this is not in the category of challah of chutz la'aretz eat and go, as Beit Yosef wrote in the name of Mordechai: where he forgot on Yom Tov and did not separate their challah — in this there is no permission to rely on leaving matzah to be eat and afterward separate; for this applies only if the dough was kneaded together; not so in matzot where each dough was kneaded alone — they do not have this law; nevertheless Rosh first chapter of Beitzah that surrounding is not required deals when he baked only one dough that has the measure and divided it into matzot — in this surrounding is not required; but in Tur one cannot say so, for he wrote: and if it is known there was in the dough the measure for challah and he forgot to separate challah until after baking, etc. — behold he does not deal with separating from one dough for its fellow — for otherwise why mention forgetting; rather it is simple he deals only with repairing that dough that he forgot to separate; and he says about this that he must bring close — meaning surrounding; and afterward he said challah of chutz la'aretz eat and go, etc.; and I have no way to settle Tur's words except in this way: he does not hold what Rosh wrote first chapter of Beitzah that surrounding is not required — rather surrounding is required even in challah of chutz la'aretz; and one may explain that law of challah of chutz la'aretz eat and go and afterward separate: there, when he begins to eat those doughs he sets his eyes to separate afterward on everything, and it is like separating at that very time — and for him it is surrounding; not so when he forgot to separate and divided the dough into loaves — when he comes to separate he must surround; and so one who kneads dough on Pesach Yom Tov — he does not call a name until after baking, and then it is his beginning to separate and he must be from the surrounding batch. And that Tur brought here the law of challah of chutz la'aretz eat and go is only regarding that he separate on the remainder and he need not combine for another dough, as written nearby — but not regarding surrounding, as above in my humble opinion:
turei-zahav/2:ד: Less than the measure. He explained: and he should not knead anymore at all; and if he kneads another dough less than the measure, there is concern lest they combine afterward in one vessel and come to obligation and eat tevel:
yad-ephraim/1:_: In Magen Avraham s.k. 3 to distinguish between two doughs; and it is difficult, for Rosh chapter 3 of Pesachim, etc.; and it appears to distinguish, etc. — meaning what Rosh wrote that plain surrounding is required in order to separate terumah from the surrounding batch — that what he separates for challah should be surrounded to its remainder, even though in eat and go he requires remainder from which he separates, and to those remainders the challah he separates must be surrounded; only Tur's language who wrote "he brings all the loaves together" — requires study; see Taz s.k. 5:
yad-ephraim/2:_: (s.k. 6) Because it is fit for him — this version is not understood; see Bach that for this version one should read: adult who saw keri and immersed; or through nullifying it in the majority — see there:
mishnah-berurah/1:ז: (7) In basket — large basket bring together touching; if each has challah measure, Rama below: no basket needed, touching suffices; house combines without vessels; can separate one for another; if in vessels, bring vessels together open above [closed even close does not help] — when each has measure; if not each has measure, need combination — no leniency open close unless one basket or cloth cover — Biur Halacha.
mishnah-berurah/2:ב: (15) He may not bake it — no food need this baking; only if owner called name; another even if calls — no right to separate terumah. Servant in house — Yoreh De'ah 328 Acharonim.
